mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates economic weakness, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth by more than 1% over two quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% in a month signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% in a month, it signals a strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% and RSAFS increases > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS increases on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between PAYEMS decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals inflationary pressure and potential monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS > 2%
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of CPIAUCSL increases and high FEDFUNDS on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% over two quarters signals a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between GDPC1 increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
